It should be performed in such a manner that the guru indeed attains pleasure; / for the guru was created by the Creator for the deliverance of living beings.

Therefore, worship of the guru must indeed be performed with great care. / He who destroys what is unfavorable and always shows what is beneficial to oneself,

he is the guru, and he should be known as one skilled in the meaning of all dharma. / Without practicing deceit regarding wealth, one should present that to the guru.

When presented to the guru, O king, the vow becomes complete. / Having performed the midday rite, eating in the company of brāhmaṇas

should be done, O tiger among kings, and the day should be passed with sacred stories. / Whoever undertakes the Unmīlanī vow in according with this rule,

6.36.m:
dwells in the presence of Viṣṇu for thousands of millions of kalpas.

Nārada said: / What is that called Pakṣavarddhanī like, O Mahādeva, / through the observance of which a living being is freed from great sin?

The glorious Mahādeva said: / If the new moon day becomes completely filled during the day, / and becoming sixty nāḍikās, extends into the day of Pratipad, / that becomes Pakṣavarddhinī, equal to ten thousand horse sacrifices.
Nārada said: / I ask now about the ritual of worship, O best of gods, / by performing which, O Mahādeva, one attains great fruit.
Mahādeva said: / I shall now declare the ritual of worship, O delight of the twice-born. / When Viṣṇu is worshipped and venerated, [the devotee] attains the fruit without doubt,
by which ritual of worship Mādhava attains satisfaction. / An unblemished pot filled with water and smeared with sandalwood,
furnished with the five gems and encircled with a garland of flowers, / [and] a vessel made of copper containing wheat should be placed upon the pot.
One should have a golden deity made bearing the name of the month. / A most charming bathing according to the prescribed rules with the five nectars
one should perform for the Lord of the gods of gods, the Lord of the world, the Protector of the world. / Anointing should indeed be done with saffron, agallochum, and sandalwood.
A pair of garments should be given, along with a parasol and sandals. / One should worship the supreme Lord of deities situated upon the vessel on the pot:
'To Padmanābha, indeed, the two feet; the two knees to Viśvamūrti; / the two thighs indeed to Jñānagamya; the waist to Dānaprada;
the belly to Viśvanātha; the heart to Śrīdhara; / the neck to Kaustubhakaṇṭha; the two arms to Kṣatrāntakārin;
the forehead to Vyomamūrdhan; the head indeed to Sarvarūpin.' / And [one should worship] Kamalā of divine form in all her limbs with her own name.
Having thus worshipped according to rule, the wise person should then offer an arghya / with a bright coconut to the discus-bearer, the God of gods:
'By this very offering of arghya the vow becomes complete. / Deliver me, sunk in the ocean of worldly existence, O Lord of the world!
You are the lord of all worlds, and you are visibly the master of the world. / Accept the arghya offered by me; homage to you, O Padmanābha!'
Heart-pleasing food-offerings, especially of the six flavors, / should be particularly given to Keśava with true devotion.
One should offer betel leaf with camphor to the god with devotion. / One should offer a lamp with ghee or with sesame oil.
Having performed [this] according to proper procedure, one should arrange for the worship of the guru. / One should give garments, a turban, and a jacket,
and one should present a priestly gift according to one's means to the guru. / Having offered food, betel, and an arghya, one should present it.
According to the measure of one's wealth, or according to their capacity by the poor, / the Pakṣavarddhinī Dvādaśī should be observed with proper effort.

Then one should keep a night-vigil accompanied by songs and dances,
along with recitation of the Purāṇa, accompanied by laughter and joy.
Those who praise and celebrate the vigil of the discus-bearer / will have an unbroken festival in their house for ten lives.
Therefore, this most blessed Pakṣavarddhanī must be observed; / by performing it, one attains all the meritorious fruit without doubt.
Those wise people who listen to the glorification of Pakṣavarddhanī— / everything done by them is well-done until the dissolution of elements.
Whatever merit there is in the practice of the five fires and in the practice of sacred bathing-places, / one attains that merit because of the vigil of Viṣṇu.
Pakṣavarddhanikā is meritorious, purifying, and destroys sin; / fasting [on it] destroys ten million slaughters of a brāhmaṇa.
Formerly performed by Vasiṣṭha and by Bhāradvāja, O sage, / and performed by Dhruva and Ambarīṣa, this [observance] is beloved by Viṣṇu.
This is equal to Kāśī in merit, this is indeed equal to Dvārakā; / and when fasted upon by a devotee, it grants desired wishes.
This is blessed, most blessed, destroying tens of thousands of killings; / it must be observed especially by Vaiṣṇavas intent upon knowledge.
Ah, the Lord of all, the God, is to be served by those intent upon vows! / What else is to be gained by saying much? This excellent vow should be performed.
Just as the moon increases, especially in the bright fortnight, / even so the devotee increases because of the Pakṣavarddhinī.
Just as darkness is destroyed immediately upon sunrise, / so sin meets destruction because of performing the Pakṣavarddhinī.

6.37.m: Mahādeva said: / Listen, O Nārada, I will speak of the glorification of the vigil, / hearing which even a great sinner attains liberation, without doubt.
Nārada said: / Ah, Viṣṇu is the Lord of the universe, the eternal purifier! / The glorification of fasting for him has indeed been heard from your mouth, O Śiva.
Nevertheless, I wish to hear the glorification of the vigil: / What is the glorification of the vigil like, and what is the devotion in the night like?

Tell me of the worship during the watches of the night, O Lord of the universe! / You are always to be worshipped among the worlds; you indeed are the god Janārdana; / you indeed are the god who is Lord of the universe, because of devotion to Janārdana.
And you, Umā's husband, are the best among all devotees. / In this world, your renown always endures through devotion.
Therefore, O Lord of the universe, tell by what means liberation truly comes to people; / speak of the glorification of the night vigil.
Mahādeva said: / Having worshipped Viṣṇu with devotion at night on the eleventh day, a person / should keep a vigil before Viṣṇu in the company of Vaiṣṇavas,
With song, musical instruments, dance, and recitation of the Purāṇas, / with incense, lamps, food offerings, flowers, and fragrant unguent,
With fruit, water offering, faithful giving, restraint of the senses, / accompanied by truth, O chief of brahmins, endowed with proper speech and ritual action.
The man who, sleepless and filled with joy, always performs this, / is freed from all sins and becomes dear to Viṣṇu.
When the night vigil arrives, [if] Vaiṣṇavas sleep, / they forfeit the fast and the vow named after Viṣṇu.
Those men, O wise one, who keep the vigil called Viṣṇu's / with a devotional mindset toward Kṛṣṇa, and never sleep,
And who repeatedly utter the name of Kṛṣṇa with their minds, / should be known as the most blessed, especially on this night.
At every moment, it equals the gift of a cow; in each ghaṭī, it is fourfold; / in each three-hour watch, it is multiplied by ten million; in the four watches, it is beyond count.
Even for half an instant of vigil before Keśava especially, / the fruit is multiplied ten million times; there is no counting it.
The best of men who dances before Keśava / does not lose that fruit from his birth until his death.
Accompanied by wonder and enthusiasm, free from sinful talk and the like, / joined with circumambulation, preceded by prostration,
Accompanied by the waving of lights with an untroubled mind, / watch by watch, O fortunate one, one should perform the waving of lamps for Hari.
Endowed with twenty-six qualities, a vigil on the eleventh day / which a man performs with devotion—he is not born again on earth.
He who thus performs the vigil on the day of Viṣṇu with devotion, / free from financial deceit, merges into the Supreme Self.
A wealthy man who performs the vigil with financial deceit / has surely ruined his soul like a wicked gambler.
When the vigil of Viṣṇu arrives, he who mocks it / is born as a worm in feces for sixty thousand years.
A brahmin learned in the Vedas who, especially during dancing, / engages in mockery—he is indeed called an outcaste.
He who keeps the vigil for an instant or even half an instant / attains the imperishable state of dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation.
Though always devoted to the Vedas and scriptures, always an offerer of sacrifices, / when the night vigil arrives, if he engages in reviling, he goes down to ruin.
One who performs my worship while intent on reviling Viṣṇu / falls into hell along with twenty-one generations of his family.

Viṣṇu is Śiva, Śiva is Viṣṇu; one form existing in two ways.
Therefore one should never disparage in any way.
Bitten by the serpent of Kali, they sleep on the day of the slayer of Madhu.
Deluded by māyā, they do not keep the vigil at all. / Those for whom the eleventh day arrives without a vigil in the Kali age,
Are ruined, there is no doubt, because life is uncertain. / The pair of eyes is indeed elevated and gives the Vaiṣṇava state,
By which sinners behold the vigil of Hari. / In the absence of a reciter, one should then arrange for singing and dancing;
When a reciter is present, O divine seer, one should first recite the Purāṇa. / [Equal to] a thousand horse sacrifices and ten thousand Vājapeya sacrifices,
The merit is ten million times greater, dear child, when the vigil of Viṣṇu is performed. / On the paternal side, the maternal side, and the wife's side, O brahmin,
One delivers these families by performing the vigil of Hari. / If on an overlapping day of fasting one keeps a vigil and performs the worship of Hari,
Gifts and all else are in vain, just as what is done for ungrateful men. / If the vigil is undertaken on an overlapping day of fasting,
Viṣṇu leaves that place, casting a curse, and departs. / Those who perform the vigil on an un-overlapped day of Viṣṇu,
In their midst Hari indeed dances, being pleased. / For as many days as one keeps a vigil before Keśava,
For that many cosmic ages he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. / For as many days as one lives without the vigil of Hari,
For that many thousands of years he does not turn back from the Raurava hell. / Sleeping on the eleventh day without the vigil of Hari,
Or staying like a mute without singing or reciting— / muteness for seven births arises from not keeping the vigil of Hari.
The foolish-minded one who does not dance before Hari during the vigil— / know that lameness will be his for seven births, O brahmin.
He who, on the other hand, performs singing and dancing during the vigil of Hari— / the state of Brahmā and my own, and truly that of Viṣṇu, belong to him.
The Vaiṣṇava who, devoted to Viṣṇu's vigil, awakens people, / shall dwell for a long time in Vaikuṇṭha together with his ancestors.
The man who applies his mind toward the vigil of Hari / shall dwell in Śvetadvīpa for sixty thousand years.
Whatever sin is committed by humans in ten million births, / it all perishes during the night vigil of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, O brahmin.
For those who keep vigil before a Śālagrāma stone, / watch by watch, the fruit is declared to arise from ten million lunar fasts.
When the day of Viṣṇu arrives, for those who do not keep the vigil / and revile Vaiṣṇavas, their deeds become futile.
Desire, wealth, prosperity, sons, fame, and eternal worlds / cannot be obtained by ten thousand sacrifices without the vigil of the twelfth day.
He whose mind does not turn toward the vigil on the twelfth day / has no right at all to the worship of Keśava.
As many steps as one takes toward the abode of Keśava / to keep vigil, they equal horse sacrifices for the one who goes.
As much dust as falls upon the feet on the ground of those going, / for that many thousands of years the keeper of vigil dwells in heaven.
Therefore, one should go from one's house to Keśava's abode for the vigil / on every twelfth day to destroy impurities in the Kali age.
Accompanied by speaking ill of others, devoid of serenity of mind, / devoid of scripture, lacking celestial music, and likewise devoid of lamps,
Lacking worship according to one's means, indifferent, accompanied by reviling, / and especially joined with quarrel—the vigil is considered of nine [flawed] kinds.
The vigil that is accompanied by scripture, joined with dance and celestial music, / accompanied by musical instruments, endowed with rhythm, having lamps and sweet drinks,
Joined with recitations as prescribed, imbued with devotion, / clear, bringing satisfaction, captivating, and delighting people,
Endowed with twelve qualities, dear to Mādhava— / that vigil should be performed with effort in both the bright and dark fortnights.
What use are many vows performed? What use to him is living at a sacred ford / if, when the day of the twelfth arrives, he does not keep the vigil of Hari?
He who, though fatigued on the road during a journey, O brahmin, / does not abandon the vigil of Vāsudeva on the twelfth day, is dear to me.
My devotee who, deluded by sin, does not keep the vigil of Hari— / his worship of me is useless; he does not worship what is worshipped by me.
He is neither a Śaiva nor a Saura; he is neither a Śākta nor a worshipper of Gaṇeśa. / He who eats on the day of Viṣṇu should be known as worse than a beast.
What is displeasing has indeed been done by that wicked sinner / who, relying on the strength of devotion to me, eats on Hari's day.
Though his body inside and out is enveloped by ten million sins, / those who keep vigil on Viṣṇu's day are liberated.
An elbow [thrust] was given by him to the messengers of Yama and to Yama, / having kept the vigil of Viṣṇu, an unoverlapping dvādaśī vow.
All desire for heaven has been abandoned by him, O best of sages, without doubt; / the happiness of hell was chosen by making Hari's day overlapping.
The ancestors were struck down by him, and the gods were slain; / the kingdom was given to the daityas by observing Hari's day while overlapping.
He who dances delighted in heart, clapping his hands, / singing with his mouth, and showing many spectacles,
Standing in vigil at night before Vāsudeva, / reciting the deeds of Kṛṣṇa, delighting the assemblies of Vaiṣṇavas,
Playing instruments with his mouth, his bodily hair bristling with joy, / portraying various attendants, carrying on spontaneous conversations,
Whatever man maintains these states of feeling during the vigil of Hari, / at every moment his merit is remembered to be equal to the fruit of ten million pilgrimage places.
He who, with an undisturbed mind, offers incense and the wave-offering of lamps to Hari / during the night of vigil, becomes the sovereign of the seven continents.
Whatever sins there are, even equal to the murder of a brahmin, / from keeping the vigil on Kṛṣṇa's day, they dissolve away piece by piece.
On one side are all the sacrifices complete with the best sacrificial fees; / on the other side is the vigil of the God of gods, dear to Kṛṣṇa.
There are Kāśī, Puṣkara, Prayāga, Naimiṣa, and Gayā; / the great sacred region of Śālagrāma, and the forest of Arbuda;
Puṣkara, Mathurā, and indeed all sacred pilgrimage sites there, / the sacrifices, and the four Vedas—they all go to Hari's vigil.
The Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Tāpī, Yamunā, and Śatadrū, / the Candrabhāgā and Vitastā—all the rivers are indeed there.
The lakes, pools, and all the oceans indeed / go to Kṛṣṇa's vigil on the eleventh day, O best of the twice-born.
Desirable even to the gods are those men who, at Kṛṣṇa's vigil, / dance, sing, and rejoice with the sound of the vīṇā.
Having thus kept vigil and worshipped the great Hari, / having broken the fast on the twelfth day according to one's ability together with the Vaiṣṇavas—
Mahādeva said: / Listen, O Brahmā, I shall declare the supreme glorification of dvādaśī; / dvādaśī should always be known as granting sons and granting liberation.
Having bathed in the morning and worshipped Hari, one should dedicate the fast: / 'For one blinded by the darkness of ignorance, through this vow, O Keśava,
be gracious, turn a pleased face toward me, and grant the vision of knowledge.' / Then one should break the fast as appropriately as possible thereafter.
After this, one should act as one pleases and according to rule. / But when dvādaśī is short and breaking the fast cannot happen by day, O twice-born,
then breaking the fast should be done at night by one desiring liberation; / then there would be no fault of the night, nor is it forbidden in any case.
As for what is said: 'One should not bathe at night, nor eat in the dead of night,' / one should perform the rite like daytime during the first or last watch [of the night].
When dvādaśī is very short on the day of breaking the fast, / at dawn one should perform both the morning and noon rituals.
The merit of that man by whom dvādaśī is always observed on earth— / I am not capable of declaring it in full.
Having attained all their desires, great men reach [the goal]— / all those such as Ambarīṣa who are celebrated devotees on earth.
Having observed dvādaśī, they went to Viṣṇu's abode. / True, true, again true is what has been spoken by me to you!
There is no god equal to Viṣṇu, no lunar day equal to dvādaśī. / What is given here, what is eaten, and whatever worship or the like is done—
all of that attains completeness when Mādhava is worshipped. / What more is there to say? Hari is dear to his devotees;
he grants all desires until the dissolution of the elements. / And whatever is given on dvādaśī becomes fruitful.
What is given at Kurukṣetra never becomes fruitless; / likewise what is given on dvādaśī, O best of divine sages.
